memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And they made from pure gold the articles for the table - its plates and dishes and bowls and its jars for the pouring out of drink offerings." - Exod 37:16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Plates. Dishes. Bowls. Jars. Ordinary kitchen items — made of pure gold.

There is nothing spiritually impressive about a dish. Its whole purpose is to hold something else. A bowl's value lies entirely in what it carries.

Paul uses exactly this picture: we have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that this all-surpassing power is from God and not from us (2 Cor 4:7). He also speaks of vessels in a large house, some for special purposes, and says that anyone who cleanses themselves will be an instrument for noble purposes, made holy, useful to the Master (2 Tim 2:20-21).

Notice the two things that made these vessels valuable. They were made of pure material, and they were set apart for one use. A gold bowl used to feed animals would have been a tragedy.

That is what holiness actually means — not being impressive, but being set apart for the Master's use.

You may feel like a plate rather than an ark. Fine. The plate sat in God's house, made of the same gold, doing exactly what God intended.

Be clean, be available, and let God decide what you carry.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you measure your worth by how impressive your role is?
2. What is God asking you to carry right now?
3. Is there anything that needs cleaning out to make you more useful to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me clean and available. I am content to be a simple vessel in Your house. Amen.
